_readme: YOU PROBABLY DO NOT NEED THIS FILE ANY MORE.
The projected grade now arms ITSELF. The server fits a rule from the Pick
Study's own bucket tables — same two filters the page tells you to read by
eye: not thin, and holds in both halves — and re-checks after every EOD
freeze. Nothing arms until the window holds enough graded picks, so the old
guarantee stands: no projection is made without evidence behind it.
See the Calibration block on /scanner?tab=pickstudy for the buttons, and
server-v2/_lib-pick-grade.cjs -> fitRule() for what it will and will not do.
COPY THIS FILE TO pick-proj-rule.json ONLY TO PIN A RULE BY HAND.
Its presence also PINS: while it exists the auto-fit still runs and still
reports what it found, but it will not overwrite what you wrote. Delete the
file to hand control back.
`pts` is added to `base` when a pick falls in that bucket; the total is
clamped to 0-100 and mapped through the same letter bands as the real grade
(A+ >= 85, A >= 72, B >= 58, C >= 44, D >= 28, F below), so 'projected B' and
'actual B' are directly comparable in the calibration table.
Build `terms` from the Pick Study tab (/scanner?tab=pickstudy): take only
buckets that are NOT marked thin and that show a green check in the Holds
column, hit the tiny 'term' button on each row, and paste the results here.
A bucket that does not hold in both halves of the window is not a finding.
Retuning is safe: projections are stamped at capture and never recomputed,
so old predictions stay as they were and calibration stays a real test.
Env var GEX_CHANGE_TOP_PROJ_RULE takes the same JSON and wins over this file.
Auto-fit knobs (env): GEX_CHANGE_TOP_AUTOFIT=0 turns the nightly fit off,
GEX_CHANGE_TOP_FIT_DAYS (90) sets the window it measures,
GEX_CHANGE_TOP_FIT_MIN_PICKS (150) the graded picks required before it arms,
GEX_CHANGE_TOP_FIT_MIN_LIFT (6) the smallest lift worth encoding,
GEX_CHANGE_TOP_FIT_MAX_TERMS (8) and GEX_CHANGE_TOP_FIT_MAX_PTS (20) the caps.
note: example only - not fitted on anything
